messages:
maria.sre: heads-up — customers reporting higher p95 after yesterday's runtime rollout to canary (v2.4.3).
samir.runtime: saw it on internal dashboards too, p95 ~ 2x on long-tail request shapes. p50 unchanged. starting investigation.
leo.support: two customer tickets: one high-throughput ingestion app, one chat product hitting p99 tail. both started at ~2026-03-16 23:10 UTC.
maria.sre: deploy-bot shows the canary batch pushed at 2026-03-16 22:58 UTC. config change: default allocator and kernel-selection tweak enabled (flag: fast_alloc=true).
opsbot: deploy-bot: canary rollout v2.4.3 -> 10% traffic (k8s-group-canary-7). No automatic rollback triggered.
samir.runtime: initial hypothesis: allocator change causing fragmentation / slower cold-path allocation under certain sequence lengths. can we reproduce with same request shapes?
leo.support: paste of customer request payload (redacted):
```
POST /v1/generate
{ "model": "open-llm-13b", "input": "long chat with many short turns", "max_tokens": 128 }
```
maria.sre: quick repro script I used locally:
```
for i in {1..200}; do curl -s -X POST https://canary.api.redwood/v1/generate -d '{"model":"open-llm-13b","input":"repeat token test","max_tokens":64}' &
done; wait
```
samir.runtime: running that shows ~p95 latency 480ms on v2.4.3 canary vs 210ms on v2.4.2. Stack traces show runtime waiting on vmalloc-like path and mutex contention in allocator.
iris.prod: customers need mitigation ASAP. options: rollback canary to v2.4.2, reduce canary percentage, or hotpatch allocator flag off.
maria.sre: I can flip the runtime flag remotely on canary nodes: set FAST_ALLOC=0 and restart sidecar. That should be lower risk than full rollback.
leo.support: can we do traffic-split rollback to reduce customer impact while we triage? set canary to 0% and shift to stable pool?
samir.runtime: quick plan:
- step 1: flip FAST_ALLOC=0 on canary nodes (non-disruptive env var reload) — maria?
- step 2: if step1 fails or slow to converge, cut traffic to stable (rollback split) — maria/infra
- step 3: bisect commit range between v2.4.2..v2.4.3 to isolate allocator change and add unit test for fragmentation pattern.
maria.sre: flipping flag now on group-canary-7: `kubectl set env deploy/runtime-canary FAST_ALLOC=false -n infra-canary` -> rolling restart starting.
opsbot: k8s: restart jobs launched for runtime-canary replicas (3/3 restarted).
maria.sre: monitoring dashboards... p95 dropping already from 480ms -> 230ms in last 60s :thumbsup:
leo.support: updating both customer tickets: "We identified a regression caused by a runtime allocator flip in 2.4.3; mitigation applied to canary, performance improving. We'll follow up with root cause and timeline." :email:
samir.runtime: good signal. we'll still do commit-level bisect tomorrow. note for the bisect: the allocator change was a series of 3 commits — guessing commit b is the culprit (changed free-list coalescing behavior).
iris.prod: capture repro artifacts: heap profiles, mutex contention flamegraphs, and the exact request shapes (seq length distribution). please attach to tickets.
maria.sre: uploading flamegraph (link): https://grafana.redwood/graph/s/abc123
maria.sre: final note — no rollback needed for stable, only canary was affected; keeping rollout paused until bisect + perf tests added. will schedule postmortem if change goes to stable.
samir.runtime: thanks everyone. I'll open a bisect thread with the commit list and follow up with a PR to revert the allocator coalescing until we validate.
leo.support: closing customer-facing loop after next status update. :white_check_mark:
